title: Core loops
summary: Separates repeated interaction, repeated actions, and the progression engine.

title: Prototyping
summary: Compares paper and Studio prototypes; tests scope, rules, UI, fun, and edge cases before production.

title: Onboarding
summary: Teach essential controls and the loop, reach the fun quickly, and reveal future goals.

title: Introduction to quest design
summary: Quests combine an objective, a quantity, and a reward; short and long goals serve different roles.

title: Design games on Roblox
summary: Official map of design, onboarding, monetization, and live-operations topics.

title: UI and UX design
summary: Information hierarchy and consistent visual language help players understand choices.

title: User interface overview
summary: Screen UI, world UI, layouts, appearance modifiers, and interactive objects are built-in engine facilities.

title: UI styling
summary: Style rules, reusable tokens, themes, and contextual queries support consistent UI.

title: UI appearance modifiers
summary: UIStroke supports text outlines and borders; gradients can affect fill and outline separately.

title: UI position and size
summary: Official reference for UI placement and sizing; use it while checking responsive layouts.

title: Cross-platform development
summary: Support touch, keyboard, and gamepad; adapt hints and layouts to primary input and screen characteristics.

title: Accessibility guidelines
summary: Text legibility and contrast are practical requirements, not just decoration.

title: UI animation and tweens
summary: TweenService can animate UI properties between states; CanvasGroup can animate grouped transparency.

title: Proximity prompts
summary: Prompts describe object, action, and input; ProximityPromptService centralizes handling.

title: Monetization overview
summary: Multiple revenue surfaces exist; product presentation should be clear, honest, and deliberate.

title: Monetization foundations
summary: Readable shops and clear free-versus-premium rewards help players evaluate value.

title: Developer products
summary: Repeatable purchases require server receipt processing; prompt-finished events are not purchase-grant evidence.

title: Passes
summary: Passes grant one-time-purchase privileges, unlike repeatable developer products.

title: Paid random item guidelines
summary: Paid randomness includes indirect paid currency and probability modifiers; disclose all outcomes and numerical odds, and apply per-user restrictions.

title: PolicyService API
summary: API reference for player-specific policy information; consult exact fields and failure behavior during implementation.

title: MarketplaceService API
summary: Canonical engine reference for purchase prompts, product information, ownership, and receipt callbacks.

title: Player data and purchasing systems
summary: Receipt handling should record the purchase, apply it to session data, and persist it before acknowledgement; session ownership matters.

title: Regional pricing
summary: Managed prices can vary by player; display runtime product prices rather than baked-in numbers and consider transfer arbitrage.

title: Price optimization
summary: Official reference for price experiments and dynamic-price checks; do not infer a universal best Robux price.

title: Season pass design
summary: Quest-aligned tiers need clear rewards, manageable effort, a defined season, and production capacity.

title: Subscription design
summary: Design reference for recurring value; read alongside the implementation and eligibility documentation.

title: Subscriptions
summary: Implementation reference for subscription products; recheck availability, payment terms, and entitlement handling before launch.

title: Private servers
summary: Private servers may be free or monthly Robux subscriptions and let players choose their play group.

title: Contextual purchases
summary: Placement can be pre-play, in-play, lobby, or UI; purchase flows must not interrupt or confuse gameplay.

title: Roblox Shop listings
summary: Listing products can expose them outside the experience; correct receipt fulfilment remains essential.

title: Roblox earning options
summary: Overview of repeatable products, passes, subscriptions, and other earning paths; account eligibility is not established here.

title: Balance virtual economies
summary: Track sources and sinks and estimate event effects with expected value; isolated event currencies can limit spillover.

title: Analytics overview
summary: Measure retention and engagement before scaling acquisition, then monitor the impact of updates.

title: Get started with analytics
summary: Use metrics to locate onboarding, progression, feature-adoption, and shop problems; investigate causes rather than guessing.

title: Retention
summary: D1, D7, and D30 cohorts show return behavior; compare cohorts around updates.

title: Funnel events
summary: Consistent server-side step events reveal where players leave onboarding, progression, or shopping.

title: Economy events
summary: Log sources and sinks after successful operations, with positive amounts and the resulting balance; production events are server-side.

title: Custom events
summary: Counters and valued events cover game-specific behavior; use stable event names and dimensions rather than proliferating names.

title: Analytics custom fields
summary: Custom dimensions support segmentation; use the documented keys and string values.

title: Analytics event types
summary: Economy, funnel, and custom events answer different questions; live event inspection helps validate instrumentation.

title: Monetization analytics
summary: Conversion, ARPPU, and ARPDAU describe different parts of revenue performance.

title: Analytics dashboard
summary: Dashboard categories cover acquisition, retention, engagement, monetization, and performance; eligibility may change.

title: Custom dashboards
summary: Group relevant metrics into a dashboard and share through existing team analytics permissions.

title: Acquisition
summary: Accurate, distinctive metadata and a functioning player experience matter before attracting additional traffic.

title: Discovery
summary: Discovery surfaces and recommendation signals evolve; use current official guidance rather than algorithm folklore.

title: Discovery metadata guidance
summary: Original imagery, accurate promises, and distinct experience content are preferred over misleading or closely duplicated metadata.

title: Thumbnails
summary: Thumbnails showcase real features; personalization can use multiple truthful alternatives and is not a simple universal winner test.

title: Advertising for creators
summary: Ads Manager provides paid acquisition; marketing claims do not establish this project's likely return on spend.

title: LiveOps essentials
summary: Post-launch support mixes content cadence, major updates, quality-of-life work, and fixes.

title: LiveOps planning
summary: Define event goals, communicate timing, and compare event and non-event economy and engagement data.

title: Content updates
summary: Repeatable content cadence should reuse existing systems; new systems have different production costs.

title: Experience events and updates
summary: Official tools for communicating scheduled experience activity and updates; confirm current requirements before publishing.

title: Remote events and callbacks
summary: Events are one-way; functions yield for replies; critical game state must be server-owned and validated.

title: Client-server boundary validation
summary: Validate context, types, values, distance, and request frequency; prompts are also client-triggered attack surfaces.

title: Security and cheat mitigation
summary: Client-side state and code are not authoritative; protect valuable changes on the server.

title: Network ownership and movement
summary: Client physics ownership can undermine naive spatial validation; movement rules must account for game mechanics and latency.

title: Data stores
summary: Official persistent-data reference; verify request limits, failure handling, and update semantics while implementing.

title: Luau language overview
summary: Roblox's scripting language reference and entry point for language-specific behavior.

title: Luau types
summary: Gradual typing supports nocheck, nonstrict, and strict modes; annotations catch mistakes before runtime.

title: Properties and attributes
summary: Reference for configuring objects with properties and custom attributes; use stable identifiers for gameplay records.

title: Pathfinding
summary: PathfindingService computes paths and waypoints; account for blocked routes and computation failure.

title: Studio testing modes
summary: Use client/server and multi-client simulations plus device and network emulation rather than only solo Play.

title: Version History
summary: Named saved/published checkpoints make releases traceable and enable restoring prior place versions.

title: Publish games and places
summary: Places are separate scenes within an experience; publishing metadata shapes the first impression.

title: Design for performance
summary: Choose a baseline device, monitor memory/frame rate, and consider streaming while designing the world.

title: Improve performance
summary: Reduce expensive per-frame work, overdraw, and unnecessary replication; profile before optimizing.

title: MicroProfiler walkthrough
summary: Frame-time captures and custom profiling labels help identify an actual bottleneck.

title: Instance streaming
summary: Reference for dynamically loaded world content; client scripts must tolerate missing or unloaded instances.

title: Custom 3D assets
summary: Custom meshes become MeshParts; the asset's intended use determines its technical requirements.

title: Studio Importer
summary: Preview meshes, transforms, scale, pivots, textures, creator ownership, and usage permissions during import.

title: Blender to Studio
summary: Modeling and export workflow reference; set asset creator and import transforms deliberately.

title: ParticleEmitter API
summary: Emit can create bounded bursts; Rate and Lifetime affect ongoing particle population.

title: Effects overview
summary: Lighting, particles, beams, and other objects provide reusable visual feedback tools.

title: Audio overview
summary: Positional and non-positional sound can provide feedback and wayfinding; modern audio objects offer flexible routing.

title: Audio assets
summary: Use audio you have rights to; imported audio has usage permissions and moderation requirements.

title: Localization
summary: Source/supported languages and translation tables support global players; review automatic translations where meaning matters.

title: Translate dynamic content
summary: Parameterized strings preserve translated sentence structure around names, quantities, and dates.

title: Badges
summary: Reference for Roblox platform achievements; design milestones separately from paid product ownership.

title: Assistant for Studio
summary: Assistant can act on the data model, scripts, materials, and models; generated output still needs review and testing.

title: Assistant prompt guide
summary: Name exact instances, specify concrete behavior and parameters, and distinguish object-generation requests from image composition.

title: Coding-agent best practices
summary: Give the agent a goal, relevant context, constraints, and completion criteria; durable guidance and validation improve repeatability.

title: Rojo introduction
summary: File-based Roblox projects enable external editors, Git history, and static-analysis tools; optional, not a prerequisite.

title: Selene linter
summary: Maintainer repository for a Lua linter; verify the installed version and Luau/Roblox configuration before use.

title: StyLua formatter
summary: Maintainer repository for formatting Lua/Luau source consistently; formatting is not a behavioral test.

title: Obsidian Graph view
summary: Graph nodes are notes and links are internal links; groups color matching notes and forces change layout.

title: Roblox core curriculum
summary: Structured Studio learning through a small platformer prototype and playtesting.
